fixer.summary: Gave MoveMode a `crawling: bool = False` field and set it on the "crawl" entry of MOVE_MODES. move() now applies crawling's doubled cost via `spec.crawling` instead of checking `mode == "crawl"`, so the crawl cost comes from the table, like the Prone check. Behaviour is unchanged. Added unit tests: only the crawl entry is flagged as crawling, and crawling while not Prone costs double while walking doesn't. Ruff, unit tests (401 passed), the Prone/crawl glossary tests and dev-gate all pass. No SRD tag was added: GLOSS.crawling has no stage-A analysis to take a clause number from, and the existing GLOSS.prone#1 tag still covers the Prone part.

review.summary:
I'm approving this. `MoveMode` gains a `crawling` flag, set only on the "crawl" entry of `MOVE_MODES`. `move()` now reads `spec.crawling` instead of checking `mode == "crawl"`, so the extra crawl cost comes from the table, as the ticket asked. Nothing in `dungdra/` still picks out crawl by name.

The behaviour test, `test_crawling_costs_double_without_being_prone_and_walking_does_not`, checks real movement costs: 20 ft to crawl 10 ft, 10 ft to walk 10 ft, and the final position. `test_only_the_crawl_entry_of_the_move_modes_table_is_crawling` mostly repeats the table's own setting. It still guards against the flag spreading to other modes, so it's not worth a rejection. Apart from the loop's own cost-log line, nothing in the diff goes beyond the ticket.
